<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b7d99ed78fab574e313a2cde71465e6b73a5d409` — the merge of head `6e4a904ea1db76b7dc04618fb8fcd80e04bccc04` into base `f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b7d99ed78fab574e313a2cde71465e6b73a5d409 && git checkout b7d99ed78fab574e313a2cde71465e6b73a5d409
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c 6e4a904ea1db76b7dc04618fb8fcd80e04bccc04 && git checkout -B drift-repro f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c && git merge --no-ff 6e4a904ea1db76b7dc04618fb8fcd80e04bccc04

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f72f335393f40e27194c56911e6de46052cb6f4c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `33acf12ec4b1c5a7d50fe55b99864f867d9e1812`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-save-refused-without-knowledge-service.ts + packages/metadata-core/src/knowledge-source-save-admission.ts, packages/objectql/src/knowledge-source-unserved.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts, and the eleven test files of the diff (narrowing face: every path outside the prose faces). Read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the duplicate door), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`resolveServiceOrLoud`, `classifyService`), packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts (`kernelServiceProvider`), packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts and knowledge-service-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts.

Inputs: card #37983 body and all four comments (ruling 7220511579, claim 7220546046, dev reports 7222789795 and 7228132286; no earlier contract-review record), PR #38013 body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base 8d34c4404f, which is `origin/main`), and the check-runs on the head: 59 success, 12 skipped (opt-in and queue-only jobs), 0 failure, 0 pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, narrowed, right: `authoredKnowledgeSourceRefusal` answered `undefined` (admit) on `main` when `resolveKnowledgeService` answered `undefined` or `null` for a non-system writer; at this head it answers a `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` refusal. One new line decides it, placed after the `isSystem` return and the resolve try/catch and before the member check. This is the narrowing ruling D item 1 orders, and the PR declares it.
- Accept set, held, right: `isSystem === true` returns before the service is resolved (ruling item 2); a registered service with no `admitAuthoredSource` still admits (the claim's fold-or-serial line: only "no knowledge service registered" is ruled). Both are pinned at the predicate.
- Public surface, unchanged, right: the exported function's signature, `AuthoredKnowledgeSourceRefusal`, `KnowledgeSourceSaveAdmitter` and `KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_ADMISSION_SERVICE` are untouched; `noKnowledgeServiceRefusal` is module-private; `UNSERVED_REMEDY` in objectql is module-private. No Zod schema changes. The spec package gains one semantic migration entry (discovered by file name, id unique in the tree).
- Doors, right: no door changes shape. REST `PUT` passes `refused.code` through for a non-403; the dispatcher `PUT` answers `deps.error(message, 503)`; the MCP draft save passes `refused.code` through for a non-403; each is pinned with code, status, the reason sentence, the ordered remedy and a zero-write assertion.
- Derived and wider than the ruling's enumerated doors: the package duplicate door (`refuseDuplicatedKnowledgeSources`, not in the diff) asks the same predicate, so a non-system duplicate of a package holding a source is refused 503 on a no-service deployment. Declared in the changeset, the entry's `surface`, the protocol docs page and a pin. See ③.
- Boot line, right: text only; `describeUnservedKnowledgeSources` keeps its signature and its `warn`, never-refuse posture (ADR-0078 §4, ruling item 2). `UNSERVED_REMEDY` is a `const` declared below the function that reads it; it is read at call time, after module evaluation, so there is no temporal-dead-zone fault.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` appear line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. `narrowed` is the right kind ("a value refused or a requirement tightened"): an author's `knowledge_source` save that `main` accepts is refused. `no` is right: no published export or schema moves (`check:api-surface` unchanged per the green `Lint` families).
- Level: `@objectstack/metadata-core` `minor` satisfies "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves"; `@objectstack/objectql` `patch` (a log sentence) and `@objectstack/spec` `patch` (one upgrade-guide entry) are right for what those packages publish. `packages/rest` and `packages/runtime` change comments only and carry no line; nothing they publish moves except through the metadata-core dependency.
- BREAKING banner, the `!` title, the FROM to TO mapping and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered knowledge-source-save-refused-without-knowledge-service`) are present, and the id matches the entry. Both `Check Changeset` runs and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (both dev reports, PR body): keep the package duplicate door refused? Answer: A, keep it, as pushed. It is a non-system save of the same item through the one predicate; the ruling's rule sentence reads "at each door that saves one", and its reasoning (ADR-0078 §1) applies to the copy equally; a carve-out needs a new input on an exported function, which the ruling did not order. ESCALATED all the same, because the ruling's parenthesis enumerates three doors and this is a fourth: the refusal blocks the duplicate of a whole package (objects, pages, flows) because it holds one source, and the PR body's maintainer summary does not name it. The Tier H approval is where it is decided; the approver should read the "Open question" section before approving. Not a finding against this head.
- Dev flag, two door-level `isSystem` cases dropped: accepted. Inbound HTTP carries no `isSystem`; the hold is pinned at the predicate, with the resolver asserted never called.
- Dev flag, five collateral suites now mount an admitting knowledge service: accepted. Each harness change is confined to the `knowledge` name and keeps the branded not-registered miss for every other name.
- Dev flag, dogfood battery NOT MEASURED locally: answered by the check-run `Dogfood Regression Gate`, success on this head.
- Dev flag, positive live control with `requires: ['knowledge']` NOT MEASURED: accepted; the admitted path is unchanged code, pinned by the CONTROL cases, and `Test Core` 1 to 10 are green.
- Deviations (commit trailers, a throwaway dev-server session token printed to a transcript and the server stopped): no contract effect; noted, nothing owed here.
- `security_findings: none` in both reports: this review found none either. The fail direction stays closed; no accept is widened.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join is added anywhere in the diff.
- Author: `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay bypass.
- Tier: ruling item 3 fixes the landing as Tier H by authorised approval. This record does not replace that approval.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Hits file, `19.knowledge-source-save-refused-without-knowledge-service.ts`, against ruling D and its first consumer (the upgrade guide, `os migrate meta` TODOs):
- Notice-only with no `conversionIds` is correct: no key or value of the item changes, and the repair is the deployment's composition, so there is no D2 rewrite to judge. The shape matches `SemanticMigration` (id, surface, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria).
- `replacement` and `reason` agree with the code sentence by sentence: 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, nothing written, system writes held, a host-registered service answering for its own sources, stored items neither rewritten nor refused at boot (the boot path in `knowledge-source-unserved.ts` only warns).
- The remedy is real: `platform-capabilities.ts` lists `knowledge` as a requested token that mounts the service and the deployment's store, and `KnowledgeServicePlugin` registers under the name the doors resolve (`KNOWLEDGE_SERVICE`, `'knowledge'`).
- N1 (nit) — `surface`, `acceptanceCriteria` and the changeset's FROM line describe the affected deployment as one whose stack "does not declare `requires: ['knowledge']`". Since #37306 a stack that ships a `knowledgeSources` entry also mounts the service (`mountedBy: { collection: 'knowledgeSources' }`), and saves there are accepted. The entry over-includes that deployment; following it there adds a redundant token and breaks nothing. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up docs-face card.

Implementing files, against the ruling:
- `knowledge-source-save-admission.ts`: holds. Order of checks is type, `isSystem`, resolve (throw answers the pre-existing `unavailable` 503), absent service (new refusal), member check, verdict. The message names the item, the reason and the remedy in the ruled order (token, restart, save) and does not say "try again". The module doc's claim that the knowledge service answers the same code for a store that is not mounted is true (`UNMOUNTED_ADAPTER_CODE` is `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, status 503). Tried to break: an unnamed or non-object item (handled, pinned); `null` service (handled, pinned); a resolver that throws (unchanged path).
- N2 (nit) — code choice. `errors.zod.ts` glosses `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` as "temporarily unavailable", and this condition lasts until the stack changes. The ruling left the code open ("a coded refusal (ADR-0112)"), the knowledge service already uses the same code for the same kind of composition fact, and no door needs a new mapping. Accepted deviation.
- N3 (nit) — on the dispatcher transport and the duplicate door `resolveServiceOrLoud` also answers `undefined` for the `no-instance-in-scope` classification, which would be told "this deployment runs no knowledge service". The platform plugin registers a plain instance (`ctx.registerService`), so the platform's service cannot reach that state; a host that registers a scoped `knowledge` factory answering nothing for a scope could. Follow-up card at most.
- `knowledge-source-unserved.ts`: holds. The line names the same remedy as the refusal (ruling item 2) and keeps "or remove the item(s)". The module doc's account of where such items come from (a system write after boot, or a save made before the refusal) agrees with the predicate.
- `meta-item-write-routes.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `meta.ts`, `mcp-authoring.ts`: comment-only hunks, each true of the code beside it. REST `resolveKnowledgeService` answers `undefined` on no provider and on the branded not-registered miss, and rethrows anything else. N4 (nit) — the reworded jsdoc on `OpenAuthoringWriter.itemSaveRefusal` ("..., or on a deployment with no knowledge service, or `undefined` ...") no longer parses as a sentence.
- N5 (nit) — through the duplicate door the predicate's sentence is appended verbatim, so a caller duplicating a package is told to "save the source again" and that "Nothing was written" after "nothing was copied". Wording only.
- Tests: the new pins assert code, status, reason, ordered remedy and zero writes at the predicate, REST `PUT` (branded miss and no provider), dispatcher `PUT` (real kernel and a double), MCP draft save and the duplicate; the host-mounted accept is pinned at each door. The suites that mount an admitting service do so to stay on their own subject and say so.

Observation outside the diff, not graded: `POST /meta/:type/:name/publish` and `/rollback` (`meta-item-history-routes.ts`) write an item without asking this predicate, as on `main`. After this change no new draft of a source can be created on a no-service deployment, so the residue is rows that predate the refusal, which the boot line names. A follow-up card can decide whether those doors ask too.

## L1 review — REWORK (dogfood battery only); merits accepted

Head: `33acf12ec4b1c5a7d50fe55b99864f867d9e1812` (card #37983, ruling D 7220511579)

**Merits: accepted.** The contract-tier review is record 7228262724: PASS, no must-fix, no should-fix, five nits. The record verifies at tier. The predicate change matches ruling D: the no-service refusal comes after the system-identity return and before the member check. Each of the three ruled doors, plus the package-duplicate door, passes `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` through, and each door is pinned with its code, status, remedy and zero writes. The boot line names the same remedy. The declarations, levels and ADR-0087 entry 19 agree with the diff. All 62 check-runs on the head are green, with 12 skipped by design.

The l1-face changeset flag is answered. The `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/runtime` hunks change comments only and no behavior, so they owe no entry, and Check Changeset is green.

**REWORK — one item.** The title carries `!` and the body declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the full dogfood battery is owed on this head and recorded under `dogfood_battery`. That has not happened yet.
- The report says the local battery is NOT MEASURED.
- `Dogfood Regression Gate` shows success on this head, but its job reads `OS_DOGFOOD_RESULT: skipped` and `OS_VERIFY_RESULT: skipped`. The three shards and Dogfood Verify CLI did not run on the PR; they run in the merge queue.
- So no run of the battery is pinned to this head.

To close it, run the full battery on `33acf12ec4` and record it. If the head does not move and the battery is green, the merits acceptance stands and no delta read is owed. A red result that needs a fix moves the head, and the moved head needs a delta read.

**For the Tier H approval:** the contract review escalates one boundary item rather than grading it. The package-duplicate door is a fourth refusing door, while the ruling's parenthesis names three. The area ruled to keep it refused, because the rule sentence covers every door that saves one. That refusal blocks duplicating a whole package because of one source, and the body's maintainer summary does not mention it. The approver should read the PR's Open question section.

Nits from the record, optional, for a follow-up card: N1 entry 19's surface text includes stacks that already mount the service by shipping a source; N3 a scoped-factory miss would get the no-service sentence; N4 the `itemSaveRefusal` jsdoc no longer parses; N5 a duplicating caller is told to save the source again. A second follow-up candidate, outside the diff: the meta publish and rollback routes write an item without asking the predicate. The same is true on main.

## 维护者速读

- 做什么：执行你在 2026-11-27T14:12Z 选的方案 D（「D 拒绝保存并说明」）。部署上没装知识服务时，作者通过工作台、元数据接口或智能体工具保存知识源会当场失败，并看到原因和修法。以前这种保存显示成功，却永远不会生效。
- 风险：21 个文件 +348/−51，大多是各个保存入口的测试，另有一条语义迁移条目和升级说明。装包、种子数据、迁移照常通过。另外，在这类部署上复制一个含知识源的应用包也会被拒，这是裁决点名三处之外的第四处，专区判定保持拒绝，PR 的待定问题一节有说明。
- 要你做什么：审批人批准即可。契约审核 PASS 7228262724，Head-sha `33acf12ec4b1c5a7d50fe55b99864f867d9e1812`；批准后座位自主落地。
